prompt: Which statement about a hedge is correct?

options.text: A hedge has a cost, such as a premium or a gain you give up, and that cost reduces returns in good periods too.
A hedge removes all risk from the position.
A hedge means you can make the position bigger.

explanations.a: Every hedge has a cost. It is paid whether or not the protection is used.
explanations.c: A hedge changes the shape of the loss. It does not remove the risk.
explanations.d: Hedging is not a reason to size up. The position still needs its own limit.

prompt: Hypothetical. You hold 100 shares at Rs 500. A put has strike Rs 470 and a premium of Rs 12 per share. The price falls to Rs 400. What is the hedged total loss, in rupees?
solution: Loss on shares = 100 x (500 - 400) = Rs 10,000. Put payout = 100 x (470 - 400) = Rs 7,000. Net loss on shares = Rs 3,000. Add the premium, 100 x Rs 12 = Rs 1,200. Total = Rs 4,200. Checked again: Rs 4,200 / Rs 50,000 = 8.4%.

prompt: Hypothetical. Same holding of Rs 50,000 and the same put with a premium of Rs 1,200. The premium is what percent of the holding? Give one decimal place.
Hypothetical. A hedged holding stays flat for a month. The share ends at Rs 500, the same as the start. The put expires with no value. What is the result?

options.text: A profit equal to the premium.
A loss of Rs 1,200, the premium paid, before any other costs.
No change at all, because a hedge never costs anything in a flat market.

explanations.a: The premium is paid, not received, by the buyer of a put. Nothing comes back in a flat market.
explanations.c: The premium is paid whatever the price does. A hedge costs money in a flat market.
explanations.d: Rs 10,000 is the loss on the shares if the price fell to Rs 400. That is not this flat case.

prompt: Spot the mistake: "I hedged, so the position has no risk." Which part is wrong?

options.text: I hedged: this describes an action.
Hedging means taking a second position that offsets part of the first.

explanations.a: This describes an action you took. It is not the mistake.
explanations.c: This is the correct meaning of a hedge. It is not the mistake.
explanations.d: The statement is wrong. A hedge reduces some risk, but basis risk, the cost and any loss after the hedge remain.

options.text: The hedge always moves exactly with the position it protects.
The hedge may not move exactly with the position it protects, so some risk can remain.
The hedge costs nothing when the price is flat.
Basis risk is the premium paid for a hedge.

explanations.a: A hedge can differ from the position it protects. That gap is the basis risk.
explanations.c: The premium is paid whatever the price does. A flat price does not remove the cost.
explanations.d: The premium is the cost of the hedge. Basis risk is the gap in how the two positions move.
